item: sync-editor: "the manual syncing lyrics screen doesn't work on iPhone" (tap-to-sync editor, App/Features/LyricsSync)
currentBehaviour:
Re-verified on main 86a5cce (/home/user/pixlaudio-ios). Every line cited below was re-opened; corrections to the previous plan are marked [corrected].

ENTRY / PRESENTATION
- The root has one `.sheet(item: $router.sheet)` (App/Shell/RootView.swift:54) and one `.fullScreenCover(item:)` (RootView.swift:60-64), chained on the same view. `Router.present(_ cover:)` just assigns `cover` (App/Shell/Router.swift:84).
- The lyrics screen is itself the root cover `AppCover.lyrics` (opened from the full player, NowPlayingView.swift:312). `LyricsSyncEditorView.open` stores the statics `pendingEntry` / `pendingReturnToLyrics` (LyricsSyncEditorView.swift:32-42) and calls `router.present(AppCover.lyricsSync(songId:))`. That swaps the root cover from `.lyrics` to `.lyricsSync`. On close, `onClosed` swaps back to `.lyrics` or calls `dismissCover()` (LyricsSyncEditorView.swift:184-191), using a third static, `returnToLyrics` (l.34, 161, 185-186).
- There are 4 real entry points:
  (a) The lyrics More sheet's first row, "Sync the words yourself" (or "Fix my word timing" for user-synced lyrics) (LyricsMoreSheet.swift:85-91), calls `dismiss()` and then `onSync()` in the same tick. The More sheet is a `.sheet(isPresented:)` on LyricsView, inside the lyrics cover (LyricsView.swift:199). So the editor is opened by swapping the root cover while a sheet that cover presented is still animating away.
  (b) The sync chip (LyricsView.swift:297-298; LyricsChrome.swift:485-517) shows only for lyrics without word timing that aren't user-synced (`lacksWordTiming` / `showSyncChip`, LyricsView.swift:74-85).
  (c) The empty-state "Add lyrics and sync them" button (LyricsStaticContent.swift:202-206, wired at LyricsView.swift:257-260). It shows only when there are no lyrics.
  (d) Edit song: "Change the words" / "Fix timing" (EditSongSheet.swift:220-221, 287-290). In production EditSongSheet is only presented as a `.fullScreenCover(isPresented:)` inside SongInfoSheet (SongInfoSheet.swift:15-18). SongInfoSheet is either the root `.sheet` (`AppSheet.songInfo`, RouteDestinations.swift:51, from every song row's ⋮) or [corrected, added] a sheet nested in the root queue sheet (QueueSheet.swift:72-74). `openSyncEditor` calls `dismiss()`, which closes only Edit song, then sets `router.cover` while the root is still presenting a sheet. (`AppCover.editSong` is used only by UITestLaunchRouter.swift:241.)
- For word-synced lyrics (BiniLyrics, now the first online source) and user-synced lyrics the chip is hidden, so (a) is the only way in from the lyrics screen.

SESSION / AUDIO
- `LyricsSyncSession.open` (LyricsSyncSession.swift:181-198) pauses, begins the exact-timing session, suspends transitions (LyricsSyncPlayer.swift:57-68; DualDeckEngine.swift:259-279, 457) and suspends the instrumental (InstrumentalController.swift:103-111).
- `load()` (l.213-220) sets the default speed through `PlaybackStore.setPlaybackRate`. The real engine applies it as `defaultRate` with the `.spectral` pitch algorithm (Deck.swift:95, 210-213, 251-254).
- The real engine reports intent, not buffering: `.playingChanged(playWhenReady)` (DualDeckEngine.swift:684-687). So a stall does not flip the editor's `playWhenReady` and swallow taps as "start" presses. That theory is ruled out.
- Transport goes through `PlaybackStore.resume/pause/seek/positionMs` (PlaybackStore.swift:94-118, 158). When Spotify Connect is attached, those calls go to the remote device and the position is the optimistic remote clock (SpotifyConnectController.swift:534-568).
- `setPlaybackRate` still goes to the paused local engine (PlaybackStore.swift:151), so the speed menu does nothing on the remote. The latency correction (`rawTapPositionMs` × speed, LyricsTapSync.swift:450-453) is still scaled by the chosen speed.
- The engine's exact-timing pause-at-end doesn't apply to the remote. The device auto-advances, which surfaces as "Song changed" via `currentSongChanged` (l.337-352). It also skips songs it can't play.
- Android blocks the editor while casting: at open (LyricsSyncEditorStateHolder.kt:259-262) and mid-session (l.300-307, flushDraft + Error, no pause), on origin/android-int-oct3, with string lyrics_sync_casting "Syncing only works on this phone. Stop casting first." (strings.xml:178). The iOS port dropped that guard.
- [corrected] `attachRemote` is only called from the Connect flow started in the devices sheet (SpotifyConnectController.swift:246) and from the demo (l.814). The devices sheet can't be reached from the editor, so a mid-session attach only happens if a connect was still in flight.
- Streamed items (`pixlstream://`, Spotify→YouTube) use zero-tolerance seeks with `automaticallyWaitsToMinimizeStalling = true` (Deck.swift:138, 257-278). Seeks into unbuffered media can stall. Start itself uses `playImmediately(atRate:)` (Deck.swift:212).

TAP PAD
- A UIKit `TapPadTouchView` stamps `UITouch.timestamp` on touch-down (SyncTapScreen.swift:516-576) inside the pad, which has a non-interactive clear glass (SyncEditorComponents.swift:28-30; SyncTapScreen.swift:487).
- The first press only starts the song (LyricsSyncSession.swift:494-498), the same as Android.
- The notice pill is a ZStack sibling pinned 92 pt above the safe-area bottom, minHeight 48 (LyricsSyncEditorView.swift:69-76; SyncEditorComponents.swift:274-311). The pad's bottom edge sits 84 pt up (12 + 60 pt stacked buttons + 12, SyncTapScreen.swift:70-85). So for 4 s after each notice (`pastNextLine`, `waitTip`, removed words) the glass pill sits over a ~48 pt band near the pad's bottom edge and, as a SwiftUI view in front of the UIKit pad, receives those touches.
- Android places the pill at the same 92 dp (LyricsSyncEditorOverlay.kt:168-177, 268). But its Row has no pointer handling except the Undo Box (Android SyncEditorComponents.kt:457-486), so on Android taps on the notice text fall through to the pad.

CLOSE
- `close()` calls `onClosed` exactly once per session (LyricsSyncSession.swift:310-327: `if !wasClosed || wasOpen`). The view also closes the session in `.onDisappear` (LyricsSyncEditorView.swift:85-88). That second call is a no-op today.
- Exits that change the cover from inside a system-alert action:
  - Leave (`confirmLeave`, l.368);
  - Song changed OK (`dismissDialog`, l.360-366);
  - Remove my timing (l.398-404).
  These run in the same alert-dismissing-while-the-cover-swaps pattern as (a).

WHAT CI ACTUALLY COVERS
- Every screenshot test launches straight into the editor with `-uiTest -screen lyricsSync` (UITests/LyricsSyncScreenshotTests.swift:58-67 [corrected line numbers]; UITestLaunchRouter.swift:243). No test goes through any of the four real entry points, through a Leave-alert exit, or through close→back to lyrics.
- UI tests run `DemoPlaybackEngine` with `playbackServices = nil` (AppEnvironment.swift:105-110). So `LyricsSyncPlayer(engine: nil)` skips the exact-timing / suspend code, and `setPlaybackRate` is a no-op (Core/PlaybackEngine.swift:75). The unit test also uses `engine: nil` (AppTests/LyricsSyncTests.swift:82).
- With no lyrics service in UI tests, Save "succeeds" without writing (LyricsSyncSession.swift:785-790; App/Services/LyricsController.swift:44 [corrected path]).
- `testLiveTapping` takes a screenshot but asserts nothing about stamped words (LyricsSyncScreenshotTests.swift:36-54).
- DualDeckEngineTests has no exact-timing or rate test (test list l.39-316).
- So "passes on the simulator" only proves the editor's screens render and the demo engine accepts taps.

GIT
- Editor history (`git log -- App/Features/LyricsSync/`): fa3281a (stage 10), 940c010, cfbbac2, cf0b8c4, d68c623, 1d22211 (instrumental suspend), 5d0a233, fe07132 (always-dark palette).
- The lyrics entry (`fromLyrics: true`) and EditSongSheet.openSyncEditor date from fa3281a. No later commit touched the entry or presentation path.
- docs/design.md "Stage 10 notes" (l.412-450) and "Integrate B" (l.658-664) describe the entry points but no on-device verification. docs/parity.md row 25 is still "wip".
rootCause:
This can't be reproduced here (no device, and the owner gave no symptom). The causes below are ranked by likelihood; the evidence strength is stated for each. Overall the diagnosis is low-to-medium confidence until step 0 (the entry-point UI tests run against the current code) reports back.

1. Presentation choreography at the entry points. CI exercises none of these paths.
   (b) Edit song → "Fix timing" / "Change the words": STRONG evidence (code + documented SwiftUI behaviour).
   - The root is still presenting a sheet: the song sheet, or the queue sheet with song info nested in it.
   - `router.cover = .lyricsSync` on the same RootView then hits SwiftUI's single-presentation rule: "Currently, only presenting a single sheet is supported. The next sheet will be presented when the currently presented sheet gets dismissed."
   - Result: Edit song closes, nothing opens, and the editor pops up later, when the user closes the song sheet.
   - [corrected] The statics are not "stale" here: every `open()` overwrites them. The issue is the delayed, surprising presentation.
   (a) More sheet → "Sync the words yourself": PLAUSIBLE, NOT PROVEN.
   - `dismiss()` and then `router.present(.lyricsSync)` run in the same tick (LyricsMoreSheet.swift:89-90). SwiftUI must swap the lyrics root cover while the More sheet that cover presented is mid-dismissal.
   - Apple documents only the plain item swap ("If item changes, the system dismisses the currently displayed sheet and replaces it with a new one using the same process", fullScreenCover(item:onDismiss:content:)). Nothing is documented for a swap that races a nested sheet's dismissal.
   - UIKit's refusal of dismiss/present during an in-flight transition is runtime behaviour (console warnings), not documentation.
   - Possible results: the More sheet closes and nothing opens; the lyrics screen closes without the editor; or the editor appears and is torn down again, closing the session through onDisappear.
   - This matters most because it is the only lyrics-screen entry for word-synced (BiniLyrics) and user-synced songs (LyricsView.swift:74-85).
   - Related known bug: a child sheet's dismissal can dismiss its parent fullScreenCover (FB14007895, forums thread 757802).
   - Step 0 runs this path on the iOS 27 simulator, which uses the same UIKit presentation code, to confirm or rule it out.
   (c) The chip and empty-state paths are a plain documented root-cover swap. They probably work, with a slide-down/slide-up double animation.

2. Spotify Connect attached. MEDIUM evidence (code is certain; whether Hoa was on Connect is unknown, but owner items 8 and 10 show Hoa uses Connect).
   - Play, pause and seek go over the network. Taps are stamped against the optimistic remote clock (SpotifyConnectController.swift:534-568), so every word lands off by the Connect latency.
   - The speed menu does nothing, yet the latency correction is still scaled by 0.75/0.5. Back 5 s and Undo lag.
   - The remote doesn't pause at the song's end; it advances or skips songs it can't play, which shows "Song changed" and closes the editor (LyricsSyncSession.swift:337-352, 360-366).
   - Android refuses to open while casting; the port lost that guard.

3. "Taps sometimes don't register". MEDIUM evidence.
   - For 4 s after any notice, the glass notice pill sits over a ~48 pt band at the bottom of the pad and takes those touches (LyricsSyncEditorView.swift:69-76 vs SyncTapScreen.swift:70-85).
   - Android's pill lets taps through except on Undo (SyncEditorComponents.kt:457-486), so this is also a parity bug.
   - Notices are frequent: `pastNextLine` on fast tapping, `waitTip`.
   - Separately, the first press only starts the song (by design, as on Android), which can read as a dropped tap.

4. [corrected, demoted] Close from an alert action. SPECULATIVE.
   - Leave, Song changed OK and Remove my timing swap or dismiss the cover from inside an alert button's action. That is the same race class as 1(a).
   - The previous plan's "dead ✕" fix (always calling onClosed) would not help: `onClosed` changes `router.cover` synchronously. A second call would be blocked by the new `router.cover == .lyricsSync(songId:)` guard, or would re-assign an equal value, which doesn't re-present anything.
   - The right move is to cover this exit with a UI test (step 0/9) and fix it only if the test fails.

5. Real-engine-only behaviour that CI never runs:
   - streamed songs can stall on exact seeks (silence after Undo / Back 5 s / preview, position frozen);
   - the Bluetooth default offset (180 ms) may double-compensate if AVPlayer's timebase already includes route latency (unverified; Earlier/Later fixes it);
   - the instrumental suspend swaps decks asynchronously (DualDeckEngine+Instrumental.swift:21-60); rare.

6. Words screen ("Paste the lyrics", only for songs without lyrics): `.onTapGesture { focused = true }` on the TextEditor's container (SyncWordsEntryScreen.swift:113) may interfere with caret placement and the Paste edit menu on device. Unverified.

options.name: A. Defer every open until other presentations are gone (minimal; recommended)
options.description:
Keep `AppCover.lyricsSync` as the root cover, but never change `router.cover` while another presentation is dismissing.
- LyricsView: the More sheet's sync row only records a pending flag. `.sheet(isPresented:onDismiss:)` opens the editor after the sheet is gone.
- Router: `presentCoverAfterDismissingSheet(_:)` sets `pendingCover` and `sheet = nil`. RootView's `.sheet(item:onDismiss:)` presents the pending cover. `LyricsSyncEditorView.open` always goes through it; with no root sheet up it is a plain cover swap.
- EditSongSheet: no longer calls its own `dismiss()`. The router takes the whole song-sheet stack down at once (UIKit dismisses a stack when a lower controller dismisses).
- Plus: an idempotent `onClosed`, the Spotify Connect guard, the notice pill hit-testing fix, and entry-point and Leave-exit UI tests.
options.pros: Small diff in files the editor already touches. Keeps routes, UITestLaunchRouter ids and every existing screenshot test. Uses only documented API shapes (`onDismiss`, the item swap). The only addition to the ledger is `sheet(isPresented:onDismiss:content:)`, an iOS 13 symbol already used without onDismiss.
options.cons: Opening from the lyrics screen is still a slide-down of lyrics then a slide-up of the editor (two animations, about 1 s). LyricsView is rebuilt when the editor closes (loses its scroll position and immersive timer). Exits from alert actions still swap the cover; only a UI test shows whether that races.

options.name: B. Present the editor from inside the lyrics cover (nested fullScreenCover on LyricsView)
options.description:
LyricsView gets `@State syncEditorSong: SyncEditorRequest?` and `.fullScreenCover(item:)` → `LyricsSyncEditorView(songId:, onFinish:)`.
- The chip and empty state set it directly. The More sheet sets it from the sheet's onDismiss.
- The editor closes through the injected closure, or `@Environment(\.dismiss)`, instead of swapping the root cover back to `.lyrics`. Closing becomes a plain dismissal (no swap from alert actions).
- `AppCover.lyricsSync` stays for Edit song (with option A's router deferral) and for UI tests.
options.pros: One present animation, and back to the same lyrics instance instantly. Closer to Android's `LyricsSyncEditorOverlay` (a layer over the lyrics sheet). Removes the static return-to-lyrics juggling and the alert-action swap.
options.cons: Two close paths to maintain. LyricsView's `stopDriver` sets `isIdleTimerDisabled = false` when its view disappears (LyricsView.swift:461-464), possibly after the editor appeared, so the editor must re-assert keep-screen-on. Android hit the same issue and uses the window flag for that reason (LyricsSyncEditorOverlay.kt:198-210). More nested presentations inside a fullScreenCover (FB14007895). LyricsView already has a sheet, an alert, a fileImporter and a fileExporter. More screenshot churn.

options.name: C. Android-style overlay inside LyricsView (no presentation at all)
options.description: Render `LyricsSyncEditorView` in a ZStack overlay over the lyrics content when a request is set (Android `LyricsSyncEditorOverlay`).
options.pros: No UIKit presentation races at all. Instant open and close.
options.cons: LyricsView keeps its CADisplayLink karaoke driver and Metal artwork running underneath unless they are explicitly paused (120 Hz cost, docs/performance.md rules). The editor's alerts and fileExporter attach to LyricsView's hierarchy. Largest refactor. Edit song still needs option A's deferral.

recommendedPlan.file: UITests/LyricsSyncScreenshotTests.swift (step 0, diagnostic, recommended before the fix)
recommendedPlan.change:
Add the entry-point tests from step 9 first. Push them alone on a branch with `[shots:LyricsSyncScreenshotTests/testOpensFromLyricsMoreSheet,LyricsSyncScreenshotTests/testOpensFromSyncChip,LyricsSyncScreenshotTests/testLeaveReturnsToLyrics]` against the CURRENT code. They need the two accessibility identifiers from steps 6-7, which are additive and behaviour-neutral, so include those.
- Red on testOpensFromLyricsMoreSheet confirms root cause 1(a).
- Green weakens 1(a): lead with Connect (2) and the notice pill (3) in the message to Hoa.
This costs one CI round. If minutes are tight, fold it into the fix push instead and accept the weaker evidence.

Line 54: change `.sheet(item: $router.sheet)` to `.sheet(item: $router.sheet, onDismiss: { router.presentPendingCover() })`. `router` here is the local `@Bindable var router` (l.27), so the method call compiles.
`sheet(item:onDismiss:content:)` is already in docs/api-notes.md:196.
Apple documents onDismiss only as "The closure to execute when dismissing", not its exact timing. If it ever fires before the animation ends, SwiftUI's single-presentation queue still presents the cover once the sheet is gone.

1. Spotify Connect guard (Android LyricsSyncEditorStateHolder.kt:259-262). In `open(songId:entry:)`, right after `guard let target` (l.184-187) and BEFORE the `player.playback.play([target]…)` call (l.188-190, which would send the queue to the remote):
```swift
openEntry = entry
if player.playback.isRemoteActive {
    song = target; songId = target.id; title = target.title; artist = target.displayArtist
    phase = .error(SyncStrings.remoteOutput)
    return
}
```
   `sessionOpen` stays false. The Error screen's Close → `close()` still fires onClosed because the phase isn't `.closed`, and there is nothing to restore. Add `@ObservationIgnored private var openEntry: SyncEntry = .auto`.
2. `func remoteOutputAttached()` (Android l.300-307: flushDraft + Error, no pause):
```swift
guard sessionOpen, phase != .closed else { return }
for task in [undoSeekTask, finishTask, fixLineReturnTask, previewSeekTask] { task?.cancel() }
flushDraft()
dialog = .none
phase = .error(SyncStrings.remoteOutput)
```
   Do NOT call `pause()`: with the remote attached it calls `remotePause()` and would stop the speaker the person just picked. Cancel the tasks that would seek or play on the remote. The session stays open, so Close → `close()` restores the rate, transitions and instrumental.
3. Optional (only with owner decision 1b): `func retryOpenAfterRemote()`: `guard case .error = phase, !sessionOpen else { return }; phase = .closed; open(songId: songId, entry: openEntry)`. `open` guards `phase == .closed` (l.182), so the reset is required.
4. [corrected] Leave `close()` (l.310-327) as is. Dropping the `!wasClosed || wasOpen` condition adds nothing: a second onClosed is blocked by the view's `router.cover == thisCover` guard.

Add `static let remoteOutput = String(localized: "lyrics_sync_casting", defaultValue: "Syncing only works on this iPhone. Switch playback back to this iPhone first.")`.
- No 'Apple' wording (AGENTS.md rule 9; enforced by ci/check-forbidden.sh step 5, l.76-79).
- English only via defaultValue, like the other keys. Localizable.xcstrings doesn't need an entry; e.g. `lyrics_sync_no_song` has none.

Give `row(...)` (l.201-228) an optional `identifier: String? = nil`, applied as `.accessibilityIdentifier` on the Button when non-nil. Pass `identifier: "lyricsMore.syncYourself"` for the sync row (l.86-91). The row's text combines with the SF Symbol into the button label, so a label query is fragile.
`LyricsSyncChip` (l.485-517): add `.accessibilityIdentifier("lyrics.syncChip")` to the main Button (the one with onTap) for the UI tests.

1. Add `@State private var openSyncAfterMoreSheet = false`.
2. Line 199: `.sheet(isPresented: $showMoreSheet, onDismiss: { if openSyncAfterMoreSheet { openSyncAfterMoreSheet = false; syncYourselfAction?() } }) { moreSheet }`.
3. In `moreSheet` (l.370): pass `onSyncYourself: syncYourselfAction == nil ? nil : { openSyncAfterMoreSheet = true }`. The row still calls `dismiss()` and then this closure, which now only sets the flag.
4. Keep the chip and empty-state paths calling `syncYourselfAction` directly (a plain documented cover swap).
5. [corrected] Leave `onSave` alone: an alert requested while the sheet dismisses is held by SwiftUI's single-presentation queue, and it is outside this item.
This file also changes for owner items 1 (remove the Synced/Static buttons) and 11 (always keep the screen on, glass in lyrics). Land these in one branch or rebase carefully: l.188-194 and 449-464 are shared.

`openSyncEditor` (l.287-290): remove `dismiss()` and keep `LyricsSyncEditorView.open(songId: song.id, router: router, entry: entry)`, which now defers.
- The router sets `sheet = nil`. That takes down the root song sheet, or the root queue sheet with its nested song-info sheet, plus the Edit-song cover on top in one UIKit dismissal (UIViewController.dismiss: a lower controller dismisses all above it).
- The root sheet's onDismiss then presents the editor.
- When EditSongSheet is the root cover (`AppCover.editSong`, UI tests only), `router.sheet` is nil, so it is a plain cover swap.
- Unsaved form edits are discarded, the same as today's `dismiss()`.

Low priority, unverified: remove `.onTapGesture { focused = true }` (l.113) so the TextEditor (UITextView) owns caret, selection and the Paste menu. It already fills the panel apart from the 18 pt padding (l.110-111). Check the syncWords shot is unchanged.

1. `testRemoteOutputBlocksOpen`:
   - `let remote = SpotifyConnectStoreTests.FakeRemote()` (AppTests/SpotifyConnectStoreTests.swift:10). Keep it in a local for the whole test: PlaybackStore holds it weakly (PlaybackStore.swift:33).
   - `playback.attachRemote(remote, name: "Echo", isPlaying: false)`, then `open`.
   - Assert `phase == .error(SyncStrings.remoteOutput)` and `remote.calls` is empty (no queue, pause or seek sent).
2. `testRemoteAttachMidSessionDoesNotPauseTheDevice`: open normally on the demo engine, wait for `.intro`, attach the fake, call `remoteOutputAttached()`. Assert the error phase and that `remote.calls` has no "pause". Then `close()` → `onClosed` fires once.
3. Router unit test (next to LaunchConfigurationTests.swift:87, which builds `Router(launch:)`):
   - `presentCoverAfterDismissingSheet` with a sheet up sets `sheet = nil` and leaves `cover` nil until `presentPendingCover()`;
   - with no sheet it sets `cover` at once;
   - `present(AppSheet)` clears `pendingCover`.

Add a row next to l.196: `View.sheet(isPresented:onDismiss:content:)` | 13 | /documentation/swiftui/view/sheet(ispresented:ondismiss:content:) | `LyricsView` More sheet (opens the sync editor after the sheet is gone) |. The symbol is already used without onDismiss but has no ledger row.

Stage 10 notes, 'Entry points' (l.439-441): record the More sheet onDismiss deferral, `Router.presentCoverAfterDismissingSheet` / `pendingCover` (Edit song, queue → song info → Edit song), the idempotent onClosed guard, the Spotify Connect guard (open and mid-session, no remote pause), the notice pill hit-testing, and the new test ids (lyricsMore.syncYourself, lyrics.syncChip; tests testOpensFromLyricsMoreSheet / testOpensFromSyncChip / testLeaveReturnsToLyrics).

Row 25: append 'entry points fixed (deferred presentation; Edit song no longer waits for the song sheet to close), Spotify Connect guard (Android cast guard), notice lets taps through; feel still to be checked on the phone'.

risks: The diagnosis is unconfirmed: the owner gave no symptom. If the editor does open and the failure is inside it (no sound, wrong timing on Connect, taps eaten by the notice), the presentation fix alone won't be what Hoa noticed. Ship the robustness fixes together and send the questions below in the same message. Step 0 turns 1(a) from a guess into evidence.

`onDismiss` timing isn't documented beyond 'when dismissing'. If SwiftUI ran it before the dismissal animation ended, the More-sheet path could still race. The new UI test catches that on the simulator. Fallback: option B (nested cover), or deferring one runloop is NOT a fix.

onDismiss on the root `.sheet(item:)` also runs on interactive swipe-down and on A→B sheet swaps. `pendingCover` is only set by the new router method and is cleared in `present(_ sheet:)`, so that's safe.
EditSongSheet path: the deferred open discards unsaved edits in the Edit song form, the same as today's `dismiss()`.

The `router.cover == .lyricsSync(songId:)` guard in `onClosed` is load-bearing once `fromLyrics` is captured locally. Without it, the `.onDisappear` close would no longer be a no-op and could dismiss the freshly presented `.lyrics` cover.

Exits from alert actions (Leave, Song changed OK, Remove my timing) still swap the cover inside an alert action. testLeaveReturnsToLyrics covers Leave only. If it fails, prefer option B for the lyrics path: close becomes a plain dismissal.

With option B (nested cover), LyricsView.stopDriver resets isIdleTimerDisabled after the editor appeared (LyricsView.swift:461-464), so the screen can lock mid-sync. The editor must re-assert keep-screen-on, as Android does with the window flag (LyricsSyncEditorOverlay.kt:198-210). Owner item 11 (always keep the display on in lyrics) touches the same lines; coordinate.
LyricsView.swift is also edited for owner items 1 and 11 (and lyrics-page glass). Merge conflicts are likely if done on separate branches.

Hit-testing change on the notice pill: the Undo pill (canUndo) still blocks a ~48 pt band for 4 s. Android blocks only the Undo button itself. A finer SwiftUI version (only the Button hittable) is possible but whether the glass background hit-tests is unverified. Moving the pill above the pad changes Android-parity layout (owner decision 3).
The Connect guard is a behaviour change versus the current iOS build. If Hoa wants to sync while listening on an Echo, blocking will look like 'still broken'. Ask (owner decision 1).
Do not call `pause()` in `remoteOutputAttached()`: `PlaybackStore.pause()` routes to `remotePause()` (PlaybackStore.swift:100-103) and would stop the speaker the person just chose.
No Mac: verify only through CI screenshots plus Hoa's phone. Batch the fix into one push after step 0 (two CI rounds total).
ownerDecisions: While a Spotify Connect speaker is playing, what should 'Sync the words yourself' do? (a) Show the message 'Syncing only works on this iPhone. Switch playback back to this iPhone first.' with a Close button (what Android does while casting). (b) Same message plus a 'Play on this iPhone' button: it stops the speaker, carries on on the phone from the same spot, and opens the editor. Suggested: (b).

How should the editor open from the lyrics screen? (a) Keep it as its own full-screen page: lyrics slides away, then the editor slides up. Smallest change. (b) Open it on top of the lyrics screen, with one animation and an instant return to the same lyrics, like Android's overlay. Suggested: (a) now, (b) later if the double animation bothers you or the 'Leave' test shows problems.

The pop-up messages on the tap screen ('Wait for the line…', 'Removed timing…', etc.) sit over the bottom of the big tap pad. Should they move above the pad, or stay where Android has them and just let taps pass through (Undo excepted, as on Android)? Suggested: let taps pass through, keep the position.

Questions to pin the bug down (send all at once): 1) Where do you open it from: lyrics ⋯ → 'Sync the words yourself', the 'Make the words light up' chip, 'Add lyrics and sync them', or Edit song → 'Fix timing' / 'Change the words'? 2) What exactly happens: nothing opens / the menu closes and you stay on lyrics / the lyrics screen closes / the editor opens then vanishes / it opens only after you close the song menu / it opens but taps don't stamp words / no sound / words light up at the wrong time / 'Song changed' pops up / Save fails ('Couldn't save') / ✕ won't close / app crashes? 3) Were you on a Spotify Connect speaker, AirPods or another Bluetooth device, or the phone speaker? 4) Was the song a local file, a Spotify song or a YouTube Music song, and did it already have word-by-word lyrics? 5) Which build (the release tag or 'build-NNN')? 6) A short screen recording (Control Center → Screen Recording) would settle it.
research:
Sources (checked during this review):
- Apple, fullScreenCover(item:onDismiss:content:), iOS 14+. "If `item` changes, the system dismisses the currently displayed sheet and replaces it with a new one using the same process." onDismiss is "The closure to execute when dismissing the modal view." No timing guarantee; nothing about swapping while a nested presentation is dismissing. https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui/view/fullscreencover(item:ondismiss:content:) (markdown mirror read: https://developer.apple.com/tutorials/data/documentation/swiftui/view/fullscreencover(item:ondismiss:content:).md)
- Apple, sheet(isPresented:onDismiss:content:), iOS 13+, `onDismiss: (() -> Void)? = nil`, "The closure to execute when dismissing the sheet." https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui/view/sheet(ispresented:ondismiss:content:) (mirror read). Not yet in docs/api-notes.md.
- Apple, UIViewController.dismiss(animated:completion:): "calling this method on a view controller lower in the stack dismisses its immediate child view controller and all view controllers above that child on the stack… only the top-most view is dismissed in an animated fashion." This supports taking down song sheet + Edit-song cover with one `router.sheet = nil`. https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uikit/uiviewcontroller/dismiss(animated:completion:)
- SwiftUI runtime message when two presentation modifiers on the same view present at once (RootView has `.sheet(item:)` and `.fullScreenCover(item:)` chained): "Currently, only presenting a single sheet is supported. The next sheet will be presented when the currently presented sheet gets dismissed." https://www.hackingwithswift.com/quick-start/swiftui/how-to-present-multiple-sheets (third-party, confirmed to contain the quote).
- Apple Developer Forums 757802, ".fullScreenCover Incorrectly Dismissed", iOS 17/18, FB14007895: dismissing child sheets inside a fullScreenCover can dismiss the cover itself. https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/757802
- Android reference (/home/user/PixlAudio, branch origin/android-int-oct3):
  - LyricsSyncEditorStateHolder.kt:259-262 refuses to open while casting; l.300-307 switches to Error mid-session (flushDraft, no pause).
  - strings.xml:178 lyrics_sync_casting = "Syncing only works on this phone. Stop casting first."
  - `requestOpen` (l.236-245) expands the player and waits for the song. The editor is an overlay on the lyrics sheet (LyricsSyncEditorOverlay.kt), so there is no presentation race.
  - Notice pill at NOTICE_BOTTOM = 92.dp (LyricsSyncEditorOverlay.kt:168-177, 268) with only the Undo box clickable (SyncEditorComponents.kt:457-486).
  - KeepScreenOn uses the window flag because the lyrics sheet clears the view flag while the editor is open (LyricsSyncEditorOverlay.kt:198-210).
- Claims NOT backed by Apple documentation (treat as runtime observations): UIKit refusing a present/dismiss during an in-flight transition; onDismiss running after the dismissal animation completes.
newAppleAPIs: View.sheet(isPresented:onDismiss:content:): SwiftUI, iOS 13.0+. https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui/view/sheet(ispresented:ondismiss:content:). The symbol is already used in the app without onDismiss but has no row in docs/api-notes.md; add one (LyricsView More sheet).

LyricsScreenshotTests (More sheet shots lyricsMoreSheet*, and the sync chip on line-synced demos, since LyricsView's sheet modifier and the chip/row identifiers change)
PlayerScreenshotTests/testSongInfoLight, testSongInfoDark, testEditSongLight, testEditSongDark (song sheet / Edit song; Router and RootView sheet onDismiss change)
alternativeCauses: The owner may mean a different screen: the lyrics sync-offset controls (the More sheet's 'sync controls' toggle, LyricsView.swift:315-319, 377-380) or Settings › Lyrics tap timing (LyricsTapTimingSheet). Confirm it is the tap-to-sync editor.

Spotify Connect: the remote device doesn't honour the exact-timing pause-at-end and skips songs it can't play (local files). Either changes the current song, which shows 'Song changed' and closes the editor (LyricsSyncSession.swift:337-352, 360-366).

Exits from inside an alert action (Leave / Song changed OK / Remove my timing) swap or dismiss the cover while the alert is dismissing: the same race class as the More sheet. Covered by testLeaveReturnsToLyrics.

Streamed songs (pixlstream:// / Spotify matched to YouTube): exact zero-tolerance seeks with stall waiting (Deck.swift:138, 257-278) can leave silence after Undo / Back 5 s / preview, which feels like 'nothing happens'.

Bluetooth offset double compensation (unverified): the 180 ms default (LyricsSyncSession.swift:215) on top of a possibly latency-compensated AVPlayer timebase makes words light early with AirPods. Earlier/Later nudges and the learned offset fix it over time.
Instrumental mode on: the asynchronous deck swap on suspend (DualDeckEngine+Instrumental.swift:21-60) races the first taps; rare.
The words screen's container tap gesture (SyncWordsEntryScreen.swift:113) may block the Paste menu, so pasting lyrics seems impossible for songs with no lyrics.

The lyrics screen is still loading when the editor opens: `currentLyrics` falls back to stored lyrics only (LyricsSyncSession.swift:255-259) and may ask the user to paste words the screen is about to show.

Ruled out: buffering flipping the editor's play state. The real engine emits playingChanged(playWhenReady), not timeControlStatus (DualDeckEngine.swift:684-687), so stalls don't make the next tap a 'start' press.
